name: DLI ONE

profile.address: 8, Corporate Ridge Parkway, Sun Hill, Columbus, Muscogee County, Georgia, 31907
profile.reading:
The building at 8 Corporate Ridge Parkway in Columbus, Georgia sits inside the Corporate Ridge Industrial Park and has a history that predates its life as a data center. Commercial property records describe a roughly 110,000-square-foot structure built in 1998 and renovated in 2019, and local news reporting identifies the building as a former call center operated by TSYS (Total System Services), the Columbus-based payments processor that was long one of the city's largest employers before its 2019 merger into Global Payments. That combination, an oversized, well-wired 1990s call-center shell sitting in an industrial park already zoned for data-center use, is a common pattern nationally: large call-center and back-office buildings, built with heavy power and telecom infrastructure to support hundreds of workstations, convert efficiently into data-center shells once the original office tenant leaves.

DLI ONE operates as the data-center brand at this address, offering roughly 45,000 square feet of raised-floor data-center space alongside furnished office space ranging from about 1,250 to 50,000 square feet, dual electrical substations feeding the site with battery backup, and on-site generator capacity reported at 5 megawatts, plus round-the-clock on-site security. The company markets fiber and carrier connectivity, and public interconnection registries list DLI ONE, LLC as the operating entity at the property, with 480-volt AC power service available to tenants.

The building has drawn wider industry attention recently: Duos Edge AI, a subsidiary of Nasdaq-listed Duos Technologies Group, has been expanding a data-center campus inside the same Corporate Ridge Industrial Park, and in 2026 the company disclosed a five-year, roughly $111 million colocation agreement with an investment-grade hyperscale customer for 10 megawatts of critical IT load, with plans to bring the Columbus campus to a combined 20 megawatts of capacity by the end of the year. Local coverage has noted that, because the industrial park is already zoned for data-center use, this expansion has drawn far less public attention than a separate, much larger hyperscale project proposed elsewhere in the Columbus area. Public sources do not confirm whether the Duos Edge AI campus and the DLI ONE-branded facility described here occupy the same physical space, adjacent buildings within the same park, or are otherwise directly connected; the two are documented here as distinct but geographically connected developments within the same industrial park.

No independently published power-usage-effectiveness rating, uptime-tier certification, or public tenant roster exists for DLI ONE specifically, beyond the substation and generator figures noted above. What the public commercial-property and industry-press record supports is an active, carrier-neutral data-center facility repurposed from a large 1990s office and call-center shell rather than built from the ground up as a data center, a common and cost-effective path for data-center development in secondary markets like Columbus, and one that helps explain both the building's unusually large floorplate and its ability to expand quickly to serve hyperscale-scale colocation demand.

reading:
DLI ONE reaches this registry through a single volunteer map edit rather than any published corporate record, and the object the name is attached to is not a building.

The stored row is an OpenStreetMap area at 8 Corporate Ridge Parkway, Columbus, Georgia 31907, tagged as industrial land use and covering about 9.7 acres. It was drawn on 25 June 2021 in a bulk machine assisted mapping run that made 1,452 changes at once. Inside that parcel there is a separate object, a roughly 117,000 square foot footprint taken from the Microsoft building footprints dataset, which a mapper addressed and tagged as a data centre in August 2023. On 24 November 2023 another mapper, working a MapRoulette task described only as adding a data centre to the map, moved the identity onto the surrounding parcel, setting the name and operator to DLI ONE and attaching the website dlione.net. That one edit is the whole basis for the operator name. Because the registry ingested the parcel rather than the building, the row carries no building tag and no floor area, which is why a page built from it has almost nothing to show.

The site itself is real infrastructure. Mapped alongside the building are five metal chiller units about 2.5 metres tall and three transformer enclosures recorded at 138,000 volts. Transmission level service and a chiller yard of that size are consistent with a working data centre rather than a warehouse. The 2.5 MW value carried on each transformer object is stored under a tag intended for generating plant rather than for transformation, so it should be read as an unverified contributor estimate, not a published rating, and it is certainly not an IT load.

The operator identity is much thinner than the site. dlione.net does not serve a page. Its name servers are at leasedminds.com, its zone contact address is at jmfsolutions.net, and the domain resolves inside 108.161.208.0 through 108.161.223.255, an address block ARIN registers to JMF Solutions, Inc. JMF Solutions is a fibre, voice, cloud and data centre services provider founded in 2005 and based in Daphne, Alabama, which describes a network with heavy emphasis on the southeastern United States. That matches the single line DLI ONE gives about itself, providing data centre connectivity in the southeastern United States, but hosting a domain is not ownership, and nothing found here establishes who owns or runs the Columbus building.

Nothing in the SEC full text index mentions DLI ONE, and the Columbus Consolidated Government publishes no searchable record under the name. The honest position is that a working data centre site exists at 8 Corporate Ridge Parkway and that DLI ONE is a label of uncertain provenance sitting on the parcel boundary around it.
